newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts see Renault loss for 1997. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Renault loss for 1997. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]

text.p: Share analysts expect French carmaker Renault to lose money in 1997 for a second consecutive year, according to a consensus estimate compiled by market research firm Jacques Chahine Finance.
An official at Jacques Chahine Finance said many brokers lowered their estimates for Renault for 1996 and 1997 after the carmaker sounded a fresh profit warning last Friday.

The new median estimate for 1996 earnings per share (EPS) is for a loss of 5.8 francs, compared with the previous estimate for a loss of 3.3 francs. For 1997, analysts expect an EPS loss of 0.2 francs, compared with a previous profit of 2.0 francs.
"We're still receiving revisions," the official said.

The estimates correspond to a full year 1996 loss of 1.97 billion francs and a loss of 575 million in 1997 for Renault. The previous estimates were for a loss of 800 million francs for 1996 and a profit of 870 million this year.
For 1998, however, analysts have revised their forecasts higher, to EPS of 9.1 francs from 8.3 previously, or 2.2 billion francs, up from two billion.
Renault cautioned on Friday when it released its 1996 sales that it expected to show an operating loss larger than market estimates.

Analysts had estimated an operating loss of 1.3 to 1.6 billion francs, including a two billion franc operating loss in the car division. Several have said they now expect the car division to show a loss of around three billion francs on operations.
After falling three percent on Monday and nearly six percent on Friday, Renault shares were 1.01 percent higher at 120.10 francs at 1525 GMT.
The group is scheduled to report its 1996 results on March 20 (corrects from March 18).
